text: 2026-10-11, fifth approval, after the owner's storytelling rule (README step 4, 2026-10-11): fourteen phrases in scenes 02, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09 and 10 were trimmed or reworded so that the poet, the stone and the historians no longer speak inside the scene prose, and three dramatised notes gained disclosures (scene-05 the sword's origin, scene-09 the Shadanana-as-Pallava-king reading, scene-10 the Halmidi identification as a majority view, not unanimous). facts.json and the thirteen pictures are unchanged (imageSha256 identical); storySha256 recomputed over the new story.json bytes.

Read the git diff phrase by phrase and then the whole story.json against facts.json and research/kadamba.md and kadamba-verified.md (Kielhorn's verbatim translation, vv. 13-22). Scene-02: the sentence about the poet not hiding the word 'yachaka' is simply cut; nothing else changed. Scene-05: 'ಕಲ್ಲು ಹೇಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ' became one telling ('ಅವನು ಯಾರಿಗೂ ಹೇಳಲಿಲ್ಲ'), disclosed as the storyteller's words in dramatised[]; 'ಕವಿ ಇದನ್ನು ಒಂದೇ ಸಾಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಹೇಳಿದ' removed, and the v. 13 paraphrase that follows is unchanged and still faithful. Scene-06: 'ಕವಿ ಹೇಳುವಂತೆ' removed; the knitted brows are vv. 15-16. Scene-07: 'ಒಂದು ಸಾಗರ' (v. 17 'ocean of their army'), 'ಗಿಡುಗದಂತೆ ಎರಗಿತು' (v. 17), and 'ಇದು ಗೆಲುವಲ್ಲ' followed by the v. 18 'bore that trouble relying solely on the sword of his arm' paraphrase: all faithful. Scene-08: v. 19 (strength, valour, lineage; no advantage in ruining him; chose him for a friend) and the v. 20 pun ('ಚಿಗುರುಗಳಂತಹ ಕೈಗಳಿಂದ ಪಲ್ಲವರು ಪಟ್ಟ ಕೊಟ್ಟರು') now stand as narration; the removed poet-commentary sentences carried no fact. Scene-09: the v. 22 anointing is now told as the dynasty's later claim ('ಅವನ ವಂಶ ಮುಂದೆ ... ದೇವರ ಕೈಗೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿತು'), which is accurate, and the copper-plate parallel stays; Sircar's Pallava-king reading moved to dramatised[]. Scene-10: the Vakataka queen and the Halmidi Kakustha are stated with confidence and both are disclosed in dramatised[] (historians' identification; majority view, not unanimous, with Gai and Settar in facts.json f-halmidi-date).

No new claim contradicts the sources; every new invention is disclosed in its scene's dramatised[]. No 'ಕವಿ ಹೇಳುವಂತೆ', 'ಕಲ್ಲು ಹೇಳುವುದಿಲ್ಲ', 'ಇತಿಹಾಸಕಾರರ ಪ್ರಕಾರ' or 'ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸರ ಪ್ರಕಾರ' remains in scenes 01-08. In scenes 09-12 the records themselves are the events (the Chandravalli mason, Krishna's 1929 reading, Halmidi, Kubja and the pillar, Rice in 1894) and those references stay.

Residuals left as nits, not blockers, for the owner's next pass: scene-03 'ಅದನ್ನು ಯಾರೂ ಬರೆದಿಡಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಕಲ್ಲು ಹೇಳುವುದು ಇಷ್ಟೇ:' and 'ಎನ್ನುವುದೇ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸರಿ ಇರಬಹುದು' (both already disclosed in dramatised[]); scene-02 'ಬಹುಶಃ ರಾಜನೇ ಕಟ್ಟಿಸಿದ' (Kielhorn's own 'probably'); scene-05 last paragraph 'ಇದನ್ನು ಬರೆದವರು ಅವನ ಶತ್ರುಗಳಲ್ಲ ...' (commentary on the record); scene-06 'ಇದ್ದಿರಬಹುದು. ಹೆಸರುಗಳು ಉಳಿದಿಲ್ಲ.'; scene-08 'ಪ್ರೇಹಾರ ಯಾವುದು ಎಂದು ಇಂದಿಗೂ ಯಾರಿಗೂ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ.'; scene-09 dramatised 'ಕೆಲವು ಇತಿಹಾಸಕಾರರ ಊಹೆ' where the research names only D. C. Sircar (1939); scene-09 'ಅದೇ ಮಾತನ್ನು ಹೊತ್ತಿವೆ' is looser than the earlier 'ಇದೇ ಬಿರುದನ್ನು' (the plates carry the epithet as a dynastic title). The summary's 'ಕವಿ ಅದನ್ನು ಗೆಲುವಲ್ಲ ... ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾನೆ' is outside scene prose and allowed.

2026-10-11, same day, residual trims applied by the owner after this review and re-verified by grep: scene-03 'ಯಾರೂ ಬರೆದಿಡಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಕಲ್ಲು ಹೇಳುವುದು ಇಷ್ಟೇ' replaced by 'ಮಾತಿಗೆ ಮಾತು ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು.' and 'ಎನ್ನುವುದೇ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸರಿ ಇರಬಹುದು' cut; scene-02 'ಬಹುಶಃ' dropped and Kielhorn's 'probably' noted in dramatised[]; scene-05 commentary sentence on who wrote the record cut; scene-06 companions line shortened ('ಇದ್ದಿರಬಹುದು. ಹೆಸರುಗಳು ಉಳಿದಿಲ್ಲ.' gone); scene-08 Prehara-unknown sentence cut (dramatised[] still says ಪ್ರೇಹಾರ ಅಪರಿಚಿತ); scene-09 dramatised names D. C. Sircar (1939) and 'ಇದೇ ಬಿರುದನ್ನು' restored; summary line 5 now 'ಅದು ಗೆಲುವಲ್ಲ, ತಾಳಿದ ಸಂಕಟ'. No fact changed; every cut inference remains disclosed; facts array, NFC, no-em-dash and pictures re-checked; storySha256 recomputed, imageSha256 unchanged.

Mechanical: no em dash (U+2014) anywhere; en dashes appear only in verse ranges and citations inside facts and one dramatised note, as before; whole file NFC; story.facts byte-identical to facts.json's facts array (42 facts, same order and keys); Kannada reads naturally in the told-story register.

Earlier approvals (2026-10-10, first to fourth) covered the commentary version, the storytelling rewrite, the film sentence and the scene-05 regeneration; their fact, quotation, genealogy and number checks were not repeated line by line but nothing they covered was changed by this pass except the phrases listed above.
illustrations: All thirteen WebPs (cover, scene-01 to scene-12) were opened and compared with their scene paragraphs, imageAlt and bible/style.md; scene-06, 07, 10, 11 and 12 were also inspected in enlarged crops.

cover: Mayurasharma as king under a flowering kadamba tree with cloth fillet, gold earrings, one armlet, straight iron sword with round pommel, round hide shield, barefoot; no metal crown, no emblem. The sword has a European-looking cruciform crossguard (nit).

scene-01: thatched mud-walled homestead, square brick fire altar, kusa bundles, wooden ladle, earthen pots, kadamba tree in orange bloom, Western Ghats mist; old grey-bearded Virasharma with ladle, young Mayura shaven with crown tuft, white dhoti, sacred thread, holding fuel. Matches vv. 5-8 and the alt text.

scene-02: teacher with staff and water pot and shaven pupil with palm-leaf bundle approaching a brick-and-timber city with brick and mud rampart, moat, tiled and thatched roofs, timber gate towers; no stone temple or gopuram. Text and alt now say brick and mud rampart, matching the image.

scene-03: one bare-chested Pallava horseman in a cloth head-wrap on a small horse with cloth saddle and no stirrups, straight iron sword; young Mayura on foot, barefoot, white dhoti and uttariya; brick-timber street with awnings and onlookers. Matches v. 11 and the dramatised note.
scene-04: night, timber-pillared hall, oil lamp, palm-leaf bundle, moon through the doorway; Mayura shaven with tuft, thoughtful. Matches the alt text.

scene-05 (regenerated for the fourth approval, 2026-10-10 23:11): seated figure in white dhoti with sacred thread, no jewellery, no fillet; exactly two arms and two hands, five fingers each (checked in enlarged crops): the right hand grips the round-pommelled hilt and draws a straight iron blade from a wooden scabbard resting on his lap, the left hand sets a wooden ladle down beside a kusa bundle and an earthen ghee pot; square brick fire altar in the foreground, dark timber hall behind. Matches v. 13, the scene text and imageAlt. No anachronism.

scene-06: monsoon forest above a river gorge, wooden palisade post, small band with spears and round hide shields, defenders in cloth head-wraps; Mayura with cropped hair and short beard, ochre dhoti and sash, bare forehead, no earring, no armlet (confirmed in crop), straight sword. No helmets, no mail.

scene-07 (generated after the first pass, reviewed at 21:14): rain at night among boulders, Pallava camp with cloth tents, picketed horses, elephants with plain cloth trappings, torches; Mayura with bare forehead and no jewellery leads a small band; fallen soldiers implied without close-up gore. No helmets, straight swords only.

scene-08: timber-pillared court hall with cloth canopy; Pallava king in tall kirita, heavy earrings, necklaces, armlets, patterned dhoti, ties an orange cloth fillet on kneeling Mayurasharma with his own hands; chowrie-bearers and spearmen in cloth wraps; low wooden throne behind. Mayura's earring and armlet appear here as the bible allows from scene 8. Hanging brass lamps are plausible but unattested (nit).

scene-09: flat granite boulder beside a new tank below Chitradurga-type boulder hills; mason with mallet and chisel cutting large Brahmi-like letters; Mayurasharma watches with fillet, earring, armlet and straight sword; bullock cart. Matches the Chandravalli fact and the dramatised note.

scene-10: split frame; left a wedding procession with caparisoned elephants, drums, palanquin and plain yellow and red cloth banners at a brick-and-timber gate; right a mason cutting letters into a four-foot standing stone at Halmidi with a reader holding a palm leaf. Glyphs are AI pseudo-script, not modern Kannada and not box-headed Brahmi (nit).

scene-11: octagonal grey granite pillar on a square pedestal (confirmed in crop) before a small towerless stone shrine on a brick base beside a stepped tank; mason on a bamboo scaffold; the poet Kubja with a bent back reading from a palm leaf; coconut groves. Letters are pseudo-script, not modern Kannada (nit).

scene-12: aerial view of a moated brick city on a bend of the Varada with white birds on the water, encircled by a vast camp with elephants, tents, torches and plain cloth banners; no emblems. The camp includes tall timber siege towers that no source mentions (nit, not an anachronism for the 7th century).

No image shows a stone temple at Kanchi, a metal crown on Mayurasharma, stirrups, curved swords, helmets, mail, a lion, boar or gandabherunda emblem, a third eye, modern Kannada script or any modern object.

Fourth approval limb check: every one of the thirteen pictures re-opened and the hands of the principal figures inspected (cover, scene-01 teacher and pupil, scene-03 horseman and student, scene-05 both hands, scene-08 king and Mayura in crop): no extra limbs, hands or fingers found in any image; background crowd figures in scenes 10 and 12 are too small to count fingers.
limitations: This is an AI review by a Claude agent; no human historian or epigraphist has read the text or checked the images.

Fact checking was limited to the research files in data/history-src/research (Kielhorn's EI VIII translation as transcribed on whatisindia.com, Krishna's MAR 1929 text, Fleet, Moraes, the CIIL Halmidi page) and did not re-fetch the primary sources; whatisindia transcription typos noted in kadamba-verified.md were not independently checked against the printed Epigraphia Indica.

The Gudnapur parentage (Virasharma as grandfather, Bandhushena as father) rests on secondary reports and is confined to the facts page; the two new context facts (f-context-4th-century, f-kadamba-later) summarise the historians' general picture rather than a single primary text.

No Kadamba-period figural sculpture survives, so dress, arms, horse furniture and buildings in the images are period analogues drawn from Ajanta and Badami, as the book discloses; Mayurasharma's face and every setting are invented.
The engraved letters in scenes 9, 10 and 11 are AI pseudo-script that only resembles early Brahmi; they are not readable text and should not be taken as a rendering of the inscriptions.
The images were judged at 1600x900 WebP; small background details (crowd dress in scene 12, distant buildings in scene 2) could not be verified individually.
